explanation: Check every row, column and square region separately for repeated nonzero digits. Zero denotes a blank and never causes a conflict. This checks consistency of filled entries, not whether a completion exists.
timeComplexity: O(n²): each of n² cells participates in three group checks. The bound counts all cells and the actual seen structures, rather than treating Sudoku as fixed 9×9 input.
spaceComplexity: O(n) temporary space for one group’s presence array or set. C#/JavaScript retain sets for every row, column and block; native implementations reuse storage for one group.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/IsValidSudoku.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: A valid partial Sudoku is exactly one with no repeated nonzero digit in any required group. The helper recognizes a duplicate within one group, and the outer loops cover every row, column and region. Therefore rejection and acceptance match precisely those constraints.
walkthrough: For [[1,0,0,4],[0,4,1,0],[2,0,4,0],[0,3,0,1]], zeros are ignored. Each nonzero entry is unique in its row, column and 2×2 block, so the partial grid is valid. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: Input is a square n×n grid, n is a perfect square, and values are integers from 0 through n.
Zeros may repeat; nonzero duplicates in a region invalidate even conflict-free rows and columns.
An empty grid has no conflicts.
